records.name: Looking-glass Ray
records.note: A flat silver ray that holds still enough to double the sky. Seen only on the Glass Sea: the surface above one looks like a second sea overhead, and a net hauled over one finds nothing.
records.source: E1 wildlife seed; real species from standard natural history, numbers provisional

records.name: Ghost Lantern
records.note: A colony-jelly that pulses once an hour, in step with every other lantern in the ocean. Dead Ocean navigators time their watch-bells by it. Dried, it burns without smoke.
records.source: E1 wildlife seed; real species from standard natural history, numbers provisional

records.name: Stormglass Medusa
records.note: Rises to the surface 6 game hours (about 4 real minutes) before a squall. Carried in a jar, its colour is the cheapest barometer on a ship.
records.source: E1 wildlife seed; real species from standard natural history, numbers provisional

records.name: Bellsinger
records.note: A grey whale whose call carries three kilometres through fog. Fog pilots navigate by hearing it, and a pod answering the ship's bell is the sign of open water ahead.
records.source: E1 wildlife seed; real species from standard natural history, numbers provisional

records.name: The Hollow Whale
records.note: One white whale, older than the maps. It leads a ship through ice leads if the ship does not hunt. Appears at most once per voyage.
records.source: E1 wildlife seed; real species from standard natural history, numbers provisional

records.name: Trench Angler
records.note: Rises on the Storm Belt trench in gales, its lure visible on the troughs like a lamp. Three crews have steered to it; none returned the second time.
records.source: E1 wildlife seed; real species from standard natural history, numbers provisional

records.name: Grandfather Squid
records.note: The oldest sailor's tale: arms the length of a mast. It does not hunt ships; it hunts whales, and a ship near the fight may lose a day or more to the churn.
records.source: E1 wildlife seed; real species from standard natural history, numbers provisional
